headline: German court jails two men arrested in Aarhus over Iran plot against Jewish leaders
headline_short: Men arrested in Aarhus jailed over Iran plot
deck: A Danish citizen gets eight and a half years and an Afghan four and a half; they watched two Jewish leaders for Iran.
extended: Hamburg's highest court on Thursday convicted two men arrested in Denmark of preparing antisemitic attacks in Germany on behalf of Iran. Ali Hassan Sarwari, 54, a Danish citizen of Afghan background, got eight and a half years in prison; Tawab Mohsini, 43, an Afghan citizen, got four and a half.

The court found the two had watched Josef Schuster, head of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, and Volker Beck, chairman of the German-Israeli Society. They were convicted of spying for Iran, attempted complicity in murder and aggravated arson. The sentences match the prosecution's demand.
According to Der Spiegel, a German news magazine, Sarwari had also prepared an arson attack on a kosher grocery in Berlin.
Sarwari was arrested in Aarhus in June 2025 on a German warrant. According to the indictment, seen by Bild, a German newspaper, the two shook hands at a McDonald's in Denmark on a plan to kill Beck.
'The trial has strikingly shown how Iran exports its terror to Germany,' Beck told Bild. He wants Iran's ambassador expelled at once.
